document_metadata.title: 15、EXT. MARINA DEL REY - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Shane Falco, a retired quarterback haunted by past failures, is persuaded by Coach McGinty to return to football, citing his talent and need to reclaim courage despite risks of injury and failure.

entities.name: Shane Falco climbs out of inflatable dinghy onto cabin cruiser deck
entities.description: Shane Falco, wearing a patched wetsuit, exits his small inflatable boat and lands on the deck of his larger cabin cruiser, appearing cold and fatigued.

entities.name: McGinty startles Shane with unexpected comment
entities.description: From off-screen, McGinty remarks that Shane looks like a swordfish he once caught, causing Shane to jump in surprise upon realizing he is not alone.

entities.name: Shane recognizes McGinty and exchanges sarcastic remarks
entities.description: Shane identifies McGinty as the former Redskins coach and comments on his aged appearance, prompting a brief exchange of wry observations.

entities.name: McGinty offers flask to Shane to warm him
entities.description: McGinty presents an elegant flask to Shane in an attempt to help him shake off the cold, which Shane accepts and drinks from.

entities.name: McGinty reveals he is rejoining the Redskins and recruits Shane
entities.description: McGinty announces that he is returning to coach the Redskins and wants Shane to be the team's quarterback.

entities.name: Shane refuses McGinty's offer citing prolonged absence
entities.description: Shane declines the opportunity to rejoin professional football, arguing that he has been out of the game for too long.

entities.name: McGinty downplays Shane's three-year absence from football
entities.description: McGinty dismisses Shane's concern about being out of football for three years, noting that he remains physically fit from his current lifestyle.

entities.name: Shane recalls his negative nickname from San Diego career
entities.description: Shane brings up his past nickname 'Footsteps' from his time with San Diego, referencing his tendency to hear pressure and immediately throw the ball away.

entities.name: McGinty attributes Shane's past struggles to poor offensive line
entities.description: McGinty counters Shane's self-criticism by pointing out that his previous team lacked a strong offensive line to protect him.

entities.name: Shane confirms history of concussions during professional career
entities.description: Shane affirms that he suffered two concussions while playing in San Diego, supporting his claim of past physical vulnerability.

entities.name: McGinty makes sexist remark about football and girls
entities.description: After taking a drink from his flask, McGinty comments that concussions are why 'girls don't play the game,' expressing a dismissive attitude toward women in football.

entities.name: McGinty reveals past scouting history with Shane
entities.description: McGinty discloses that he scouted Shane during his time at Ohio State and had warned San Diego against signing him.

entities.name: Shane drops into shotgun formation at line of scrimmage
entities.description: After the huddle breaks, Shane positions himself in the shotgun formation behind the offensive line, preparing to receive the snap with one minute ten seconds left in the fourth quarter.

entities.name: Shane evades blitz by rolling left then shifting to right
entities.description: Facing an incoming blitz, Shane initially rolls left but quickly changes direction, shifting and rolling to the opposite side to avoid pressure from the defense.

entities.name: Shane throws pass under heavy pressure
entities.description: With defenders closing in, Shane sees Franklin open near the goal line, cocks his arm to throw, but is forced to dump the ball as opposing players surround him.

entities.name: Shane is tackled immediately after throwing interception
entities.description: Right after releasing the pass, Shane is violently tackled by a defensive end and knocked to the ground, remaining motionless afterward.

entities.name: New England Patriots defensive back intercepts Shane's pass
entities.description: The pass intended for Franklin is caught mid-flight by a New England Patriots defensive back, securing possession for the opposing team.

entities.name: Todd, Rod and Bob react to interception with despair
entities.description: Upon seeing the interception, Todd, Rod and Bob scream in anguish, expressing their disappointment over the turn of events.

entities.name: Annabelle collapses in emotional pain after interception
entities.description: Overwhelmed by the moment, Annabelle falls to her knees, visibly distressed by Shane's interception and subsequent injury.

entities.name: Shane is helped off field and onto bench
entities.description: Injured and dazed, Shane is assisted by teammates or trainers as he leaves the field and sits on the bench.

entities.name: McGinty stops Bateman and demands the ball

entities.name: Bateman retrieves the ball and runs onto the field

entities.name: Crowd erupts in excitement after fumble recovery

entities.name: Annabelle performs cartwheel in joy after turnover

entities.name: McGinty confronts injured Shane on bench

entities.name: McGinty administers smelling salts to revive Shane
entities.description: McGinty takes smelling salts from a trainer and shoves them under Shane's nose, causing him to snap awake suddenly.

entities.name: McGinty inspires Shane to reenter game and attempt same play

document_metadata.title: 69、INT. O'NEIL'S BEDROOM - DAY
document_metadata.summary: McGinty wants to keep Falco post-strike as Martel's backup, but O'Neil defies union agreements, demanding a win against Dallas despite risks of stadium closure, believing his hungry team can triumph.

entities.name: Augustine feeds O'Neil asparagus soup
entities.description: Augustine provides a meal of asparagus soup to O'Neil, which he rejects, leading to a brief exchange about changing tastes and mortality.

entities.name: McGinty reassures O'Neil about player's legal status
entities.description: McGinty informs O'Neil that the player, despite using an assumed name, is legally allowed to play under a work release program with house arrest conditions.

entities.name: O'Neil questions where the player will be housed
entities.description: O'Neil asks McGinty about the logistics of housing the player under house arrest, prompting McGinty's plan to keep him in the stadium.

entities.name: McGinty reveals player will stay in stadium
entities.description: McGinty explains that the player will be housed in the stadium with a comfortable setup and will fulfill his exercise requirements by playing football against NFL receivers.

entities.name: O'Neil learns funding came from his money
entities.description: McGinty reveals that the arrangement for the player was made possible using O'Neil's own funds, prompting no immediate reaction.

entities.name: O'Neil rejects soup and tells Augustine to remove it
entities.description: O'Neil refers to the asparagus soup as 'cow piss' and orders Augustine to take it away, showing his distaste and resistance to aging.

entities.name: Augustine comments on changing taste buds and aging
entities.description: Before leaving, Augustine reminds O'Neil that he once enjoyed asparagus soup and connects the loss of taste to the onset of decline in life.

entities.name: Augustine exits with soup tray
entities.description: After the exchange about the soup and aging, Augustine departs the room carrying the tray, ending the meal attempt.

entities.description: A character concerned about where the player will be housed and who learns the funding for the arrangement came from his own money.

relations.subject: Shane
relations.description: Shane throws the football to Murray, completing a pass for a first down. This is a direct, momentary action of Shane directing the ball to Murray during play, which constitutes a directed interaction captured as 'speaks_to' by analogy in the schema (where physical actions like passing may fall under directed communication in a symbolic sense). However, given the schema's constraints and lack of a 'passes_to' or 'interacts_with', the closest valid relation is 'speaks_to' if we interpret play-calling or ball delivery as a form of directed action. But upon stricter reading, no allowed relation clearly supports 'throws ball to' as a valid mapping. Re-evaluating: the action is not speech, so 'speaks_to' is invalid. No other allowed relation fits (e.g., 'favorable_toward' would require expressive attitude, not a gameplay action). Thus, despite initial attempt, no allowed relation captures a football pass as a social or attitudinal relation. The action is physical and procedural, not relational in the schema's terms. Therefore, no valid rewrite is supported.

document_metadata.title: 86、EXT. HUDDLE - DAY
document_metadata.summary: After a Redskins touchdown, Shane is injured and carried off; Franklin recovers a botched snap for a successful extra point, narrowing Dallas's lead to 24-21.

entities.description: Evans unexpectedly sprints into the play and violently blocks the pursuing linebacker, clearing Shane's path.
